claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'Qualification, IV-18' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Restriction, VI-1'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'Qualification, IV-18' then '  Restriction, VI-1'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 972 (B-60) shows the index entries one per line with indented sub-entries (e.g. 'Qualification, IV-18' / indented 'Restriction, VI-1'; 'Punctuation characters, III-18' / indented 'Format punctuation, IV-2', 'Separators, IV-4'). The markdown transcription carries the same entries in the same order, one per line, with sub-entries indented two spaces and wrapped continuations indented four ('Record description entry, III-19, IV-33,' / '    IV-34'), and blank lines at the same letter-group breaks. Every entry and page reference is present, and the main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy is preserved in the source text by indentation. The claim itself concedes the text and references match. What remains is only how a Markdown renderer would flow bare lines (no list markers, inconsistent with pages 961-962): a formatting/rendering concern of an informative index, not a content discrepancy between the PDF and the transcription.
